title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses to patient inquiries in Urology: A Comparative Study between the Large Language Model ChatGPT and treating Urologists
summary:
Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT are being discussed more and more in healthcare—for example, as a tool to answer patient questions. However, they should only be used responsibly if data protection, patient safety, and medically reliable information can be ensured. This is especially important in urology, where patients often ask about complex diagnoses, procedures, and treatment decisions, and where clear and safe communication matters.

In this study, we compare how well ChatGPT answers do compared with answers from treating urologists to real, patient-based questions. Our goal is to compare the quality of both types of answers under conditions that are as close as possible to everyday clinical care.

Study design and procedure
Patients are included during routine outpatient consultations. Their spontaneous questions are recorded, and the background information needed to answer them is documented.

For each question, two answers are prepared:

- the answer given by the treating urologist during the consultation (later written down as a text for evaluation),
- an answer generated by ChatGPT based on an anonymised case summary (without any direct identifying details).

For the evaluation, each pair of answers is shown as “Answer A” and “Answer B”. Which one is the urologist’s answer and which one is ChatGPT’s is decided by randomisation, and the people who rate the answers will not know the source. To keep the comparison fair, only obvious source hints and purely formal elements are removed (for example “as an AI model…” or greetings). The content itself is not rewritten or changed.

How the answers are rated
Two independent groups use standardised questionnaires with 0–10 scales:

- Urology experts mainly assess whether the answers are medically correct and reliable (this is the most important part of the study).
- Lay people focus more on the patient perspective—for example whether the answers seem understandable, helpful, relevant, and satisfactory.

Each question is rated by several independent people (5 experts and 3 lay raters) to make the results more stable and less dependent on individual opinions.

Main question and analysis
The main focus is whether ChatGPT’s answers are not worse than the urologists’ answers in terms of medical accuracy. Other criteria will be compared in an exploratory way. The results will be analysed statistically and will help us better understand the potential benefits and limitations of using LLMs for communication in urological care.

Data protection
All identifying information is removed before any text is used to generate a ChatGPT answer. The ChatGPT account used for this study is configured so that the entered content is not used to improve the model (opt-out). Participation is voluntary and has no impact on medical care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Diverse patients with medical conditions in urology that require a consultation by a board certified urologist
•	sufficient German language skills
•	Consent to participate
Exclusion criteria:
•	Without consent to participate
•	insufficient German language skills
